capabilities.title: Advanced 3D Cell Culture
capabilities.text: Our laboratory utilizes state-of-the-art 3D culture systems that closely mimic the natural tissue environment, enabling more accurate studies of tissue regeneration and cellular behavior.

capabilities.title: Biomaterial Development
capabilities.text: We focus on the creation of biocompatible materials that support cell growth and tissue integration, ensuring effective and durable healing processes.

capabilities.title: Regenerative therapeutics
capabilities.text: Our research encompasses a wide range of regenerative therapies aimed at restoring function and alleviating damage caused by injury or disease.

capabilities.title: Precision in Drug Delivery
capabilities.text: We develop cutting-edge nanoparticle systems designed to enhance bioavailability and targeted delivery of therapeutics, improving outcomes in various medical applications.

capabilities.title: Microscale platform
capabilities.text: Our micro-scale delivery platforms are engineered to release drugs in a controlled manner, allowing for sustained therapeutic effects while minimizing side effects.

capabilities.title: Understanding Interactions
capabilities.text: We investigate how different materials influence cell adhesion, proliferation, and differentiation, providing valuable insights for tissue engineering applications.

capabilities.title: Material selection
capabilities.text: We explore various biomaterials to determine their compatibility with specific cell types, ensuring optimal integration and performance in regenerative applications.

capabilities.title: 2D vs 3D Dynamic
capabilities.text: Our research includes comparative studies of cell behavior in 2D and 3D environments, revealing crucial differences that impact tissue regeneration outcomes.

capabilities.title: Functional Outcome
capabilities.text: By analyzing cell-material interactions, we aim to predict functional outcomes of tissue engineering strategies, enhancing the effectiveness of our regenerative approaches.

capabilities.title: Material development
capabilities.text: We focus on the synthesis of biocompatible scaffolds that support cell adhesion and growth, serving as a foundation for tissue regeneration.

capabilities.title: Design innovations
capabilities.text: Our team implements innovative designs in scaffold architecture to optimize nutrient flow and cellular interaction, crucial for effective tissue repair.

capabilities.title: Application in medicine
capabilities.text: The scaffolds and nanomaterials we develop are applied across various medical fields, including orthopedics, wound healing, Gastric complications and dental applications, demonstrating their versatility.

people.name: Dr Shatri Albertina
people.bio: The laboratory’s public research-ethics report identifies Dr Albertina Shatri as the nanoendodontic project principal investigator at the May 2025 event.
people.work: Nanoendodontics and research ethics: The laboratory report describes her leadership of informed-consent training for the Katutura nanoendodontic team in May 2025.
people.note: Name order follows the supplied roster. Public sources use Albertina Shatri; the author profile also lists Iikasha as a name variant. University works below have weaker verification than the publisher-checked journal articles in this directory.

people.name: Prof Davis Mumbengegwi
people.bio: Selected publisher-verified work by Prof Davis Mumbengegwi addresses malaria epidemiology and molecular detection in Namibia.
people.work: Malaria risk, infection and detection: The selected articles examine epidemiological risk factors, parasite-species detection and low-density infections. They document research coauthorship; they are not automatically classified as TED² laboratory outputs.
people.note: These are selected publications, not a complete bibliography. The 2019 publisher author list uses “Davies Mumbengegwi”; the bibliographic entry preserves that spelling.

people.name: Prof Nailoke Pauline Kadhila
people.bio: Associate Professor at the University of Namibia. Her public researcher profiles describe work in mycology, medicinal plants and drug discovery, including research on Namibian Ganoderma mushrooms.
people.work: Selected published work examines Ganoderma mushrooms, phenolic composition and in vitro antioxidant activity, and antiplasmodial activity of Namibian medicinal-plant extracts.
people.note: Added to the laboratory roster at the owner’s request. The publications listed here are selected work by this researcher; they are not automatically attributed to TED². A 2023 LinkedIn conference announcement independently names her, but historical roles in that announcement are not presented as current appointments.

collaborations.title: Nanoendodontics & research ethics
collaborations.summary: A lab-reported informed-consent workshop for the nanoendodontic research team.
collaborations.detail: The report places the training at the hospital’s dental facility in Windhoek and identifies support through an ICGEB-funded project. It names Dr Albertina Shatri and Dr Silas Bere as workshop leads.
collaborations.note: This is an institutional activity report, not a peer-reviewed publication. The report’s “Ms Melania Halweendo” has not been merged with the differently named roster entry.

collaborations.title: Imaging for dental research
collaborations.summary: The reference laboratory website reports an imaging collaboration connected to root-canal and periodontal research.
collaborations.detail: The laboratory describes a University of Pretoria partnership and ICGEB support. The website does not provide an independently checked partner agreement or a definitive member-by-member project roster.
collaborations.note: Shown as a laboratory-reported relationship, not as independently verified partner endorsement. No researcher has been assigned without explicit source support.

collaborations.title: Natural products & therapeutic delivery
collaborations.summary: The reference website describes collaboration around indigenous knowledge, drug discovery and delivery mechanisms.
collaborations.detail: The laboratory page links this collaboration to research into chronic infections. It does not identify a complete partner-team roster or supply a specific jointly authored paper.
collaborations.note: Partner wording is retained as published. No unverified individuals, project dates or publication links have been added.
